A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCP research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial redistribution of displays.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of CCP and prompting baselines using Llama-3 and GPT models, including benchmark results and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original model evaluations and analyses, including the benchmark comparisons in Table 2 and shot-count results in Table 3.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 retain the same counterfactual generation, answering, and collective re-evaluation procedure. Prompt templates match between v1 Appendix G and v2 Appendix F. The fuller Table 1 reproduces existing appendix content.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TempEvalQA-Bi, TRACIE, MCTACO in binary and multiple-choice settings, TimeQA, and TimexNLI-T1. The detailed temporal categories displayed in v2 Table 1 were already covered in v1.

E2.justification: The same SP, CoT, Self-Consistency, Reflection, and Debate comparisons remain. MCQA-CoT, Ret.Q, Dir.A, and CCP(e2e) retain their experiment-specific roles. V2's larger main comparison table reproduces v1 Table 5.

E3.justification: Model configurations, test subsampling, decoding settings, metrics, and experimental controls are retained. The 3-shot versus 12-shot comparison in v2 Section 3.5 already appears in v1 Appendix D.2 with identical settings.

E4.justification: Generation versus retrieval, direct answering versus aggregation, ICL example counts, counterfactual counts, prompt sensitivity, and absolute-time evaluations are retained. Moving the ICL analysis into Section 3.5 adds no analysis; the corresponding tables and plots match.

E5.justification: Appendix B in both versions explicitly reports single-run performance. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched result tables and Figures 2, 3, 5, and 6 retain their values and findings. For example, 3-shot and 12-shot CCP INC remains 57.7 and 49.8 in v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 3. The expanded main table contains previously reported results.

T1.justification: The temporal exclusivity constraint in Equation 1, aggregation expression in Equation 2, and INC definition are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims: CCP improves relative temporal understanding and consistency across explicit-event, implicit-event, and temporal commonsense tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning temporal constraints, aggregation robustness, and excessive counterfactual information remain unchanged. The shot-count interpretation already appears in v1 Appendix D.2. Absolute-time, listwise-ordering, and prompt-sensitivity limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same decoding parameters, hardware, libraries, baseline implementation links, answer parsing, and prompt templates. Scientific-artifact licensing information is retained, moving from Appendix H to Appendix G.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. Positioning relative to counterfactual augmentation, single-question prediction aggregation, and rule-based temporal constraints retains the same substance.

P1.justification: V2 moves the ICL discussion from Appendix D.2 into Section 3.5, consolidates appendix sections, and updates headings and cross-references. It also simplifies author affiliations and adds funding acknowledgements. Most scientific prose remains verbatim.

P2.justification: The main displays are substantially reorganized: v1 appendix Tables 4 and 5 replace abbreviated main Tables 1 and 2, and v1 Table 7 becomes main Table 3. Redundant summaries disappear, while full results and the shot-count control gain prominent placement. Figures and remaining appendix tables are repositioned without changing their content.

improvement.justification: V2 places the complete counterfactual taxonomy, all-model comparison, and existing shot-count control directly within the main argument, reducing duplication and making the evidence easier to assess. This provides a limited improvement in organization and accessibility; the scientific evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged.
